claim: Identity is checked against at least two identifiers (name, date of birth, number) on the band and notes; a mismatch stops everything
source: NPSA Safer Practice Notice 24 and WHO Surgical Safety Checklist sign-in

claim: Allergy band is red with identifiers on a white panel; record the exact reaction
source: NPSA SPN 24; BSACI beta-lactam guideline

claim: A day-surgery patient needs a responsible adult to take them home and stay for 24 hours
source: NHS trust day-surgery discharge advice (several trusts)

claim: NEWS2 parameter ranges and tiers; SpO2 target 94-98% (88-92% if at risk of hypercapnic failure); blood pressure bands
source: RCP NEWS2 chart (read); BTS oxygen guideline; ESH 2023 / NICE NG136

claim: Offer a chaperone for an intimate examination; explain and ask permission
source: GMC guidance on intimate examinations and chaperones

claim: Murphy's sign: pain stopping inspiration on pressing under the right ribs; local inflammatory sign of acute cholecystitis
source: Tokyo Guidelines TG07 and TG13 criteria

claim: Rovsing's sign (pressing the left lower tummy hurts the right), psoas sign (hip extension) and obturator sign (internal rotation of the flexed hip) support appendicitis but are not diagnostic
source: clinical-examination references (Lecturio, Nursing Center, textbook summaries)

claim: ASA classes, STOP-Bang bands, VTE and bleeding risk factors, TG18 severity grades, AIR and AAS scores
source: ASA classification; STOP-Bang; NICE NG89; Tokyo Guidelines; AIR and AAS papers

claim: Do not routinely order tests that will not change management; ask about pregnancy and test with consent if in doubt; no routine urine dipstick or chest X-ray
source: NICE NG45 (text read)

claim: About 1 in 20 healthy people have a result outside a 95% reference interval
source: reference-interval literature (MedCalc, Medicine Today, Acute Care Testing)

claim: Critical laboratory results are phoned, read back, acted on and documented; telephone limits
source: Newcastle telephone limits based on the RCPath guidance

claim: Sepsis: blood tests and cultures before antibiotics; antibiotics within 1 hour (high risk); fluid bolus 250 mL steps with reassessment; review times by risk level
source: NICE NG253 (page read)

claim: Medicine plan before surgery: diabetes, anticoagulant, steroid, blood-pressure medicines
source: CPOC diabetes guideline; UKCPA Handbook; NICE NG243

claim: Clot prevention: stockings or intermittent compression, pharmacological prophylaxis for at least 7 days after abdominal surgery when risk outweighs bleeding
source: NICE NG89 (page read)

claim: Deterioration clock (+5-10 heart rate per 30 minutes) and transfer escort tiers by NEWS2
source: the book itself marks both as simulator design values (provisional); no guideline states them

claim: Consent covers benefits, risks, reasonable alternatives and doing nothing; teach-back; interpreter; do not pressure
source: GMC Decision making and consent (2020)

claim: If the patient lacks capacity, decisions are taken in their best interests
source: Mental Capacity Act 2005 section 4

claim: A 16-year-old: consent follows the law for minors (Gillick competence; parental responsibility); involve the young person
source: Gillick competence and Fraser guidelines (NSPCC, MDU)
result: confirmed; the law differs by country (institutional)

claim: Hair removal only if needed, with clippers and a single-use head on the day, not razors
source: NICE NG125 1.2.4 to 1.2.5 (page read)

claim: Temperature below 36.0 degC: warm before anaesthesia
source: NICE CG65

claim: Sign In, Time Out and Sign Out items, site marking, 500 mL blood loss, antibiotic within 60 minutes, specimen labelling
source: WHO Surgical Safety Checklist; NICE QS216 statement 6

claim: Anaesthetic machine and equipment are checked and the check is recorded before use
source: Association of Anaesthetists, Checking anaesthetic equipment 2012

claim: Information lost at handover is a classic cause of error; SBAR (Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation) structures the handover
source: WHO Patient Safety Solutions, Communication during patient hand-overs (2007)

claim: Counts of swabs, instruments and sharps; a wrong count means search and escalate
source: NatSSIPs 2 (CPOC, 2023)

claim: Blood pressure below 180/110 in clinic does not delay elective surgery; do not rush BP down on the morning; rebook when controlled
source: AAGBI and British Hypertension Society guidance; CPOC

claim: Fast or slow rhythm: find the cause, ECG, adverse features (shock, syncope, ischaemia, heart failure) make it unstable; new AF triggers sepsis, dehydration and salts
source: Resuscitation Council UK peri-arrest arrhythmia guidance 2021 (overview), NICE NG45 ECG indication
result: confirmed in outline; the treatment doses are not stored

claim: Fever with a surgical source: sepsis screen; cultures before antibiotics; TG18 for cholecystitis and cholangitis
source: NICE NG253; Tokyo Guidelines
result: confirmed; the book's 38.5 degC or rigors trigger for cultures is practice, not a guideline limit

claim: Warming rate about 0.5-1 degC per hour with forced air
source: the book marks it as clinical interpretation; no guideline states a rate

claim: Low SpO2: check probe, assess, oxygen to the target range, opioid effect, aspiration
source: BTS guideline for oxygen use; RCP NEWS2

claim: Opioid overdose: stimulate, support the airway, oxygen, naloxone by the clinician
source: Naloxone SmPC; RCP NEWS2

claim: New confusion: check glucose first; below 4 mmol/L treat; recheck after 10-15 minutes
source: RCP NEWS2 (confusion scores 3); JBDS hypoglycaemia guideline

claim: Peritonitis and perforation: re-examine, urgent senior review, surgery; an appendix not seen is not a normal appendix; leucocytosis above 18 is a TG18 moderate-grade criterion
source: WSES Jerusalem 2020 PDF; Tokyo Guidelines

claim: Potassium bands, ECG changes, haemolysed samples, insulin-glucose lowers potassium by about 0.65-1.0 mmol/L at 30-60 minutes
source: UKKA hyperkalaemia guideline July 2026 (PDF read)

claim: Low potassium: replace carefully, check magnesium; planned surgery deferred below about 3.0
source: the book states there is no single guideline for these bands and marks them as interpretation

claim: Sodium correction no faster than 10 mmol/L in 24 hours (about 8 per day after) to avoid osmotic demyelination
source: European clinical practice guideline on hyponatraemia 2014

claim: Transfusion threshold 70 g/L (restrictive), 80 g/L with acute coronary syndrome; unexplained anaemia is investigated before planned surgery
source: NICE NG24 1.5.1 to 1.5.3 (page read); WHO anaemia limits
result: confirmed; NG24 names acute coronary syndrome where the book says heart disease

claim: One unit of red cells raises haemoglobin by about 10 g/L
source: the book marks it as clinical interpretation (a standard teaching figure)

claim: Neutrophils below 0.5 are a critical result; platelet clumping and haemolysis give false results
source: Newcastle haematology telephone limits; EDTA pseudothrombocytopenia literature

claim: Acute kidney injury: fluids if dry, stop NSAIDs, avoid contrast unless essential, creatinine rise of 26 micromol/L in 48 hours
source: KDIGO and NICE NG148 (page read)

claim: Duct-stone risk: high risk goes to ERCP, intermediate to MRCP; cholangitis is an emergency
source: ASGE 2019 and Tokyo Guidelines

claim: Check ketones if glucose persistently high or unwell or on an SGLT2 inhibitor
source: CPOC diabetes guideline 2023 (PDF read)
result: confirmed; CPOC says two readings above 13 mmol/L, the book keeps JBDS's 14

claim: INR 1.9 without warfarin: liver disease, bile blockage or sepsis; correct before surgery; avoid neuraxial block
source: UKCPA Handbook (warfarin, neuraxial advice); the book cites AoA/OAA/RA-UK 2013
result: confirmed in principle; reversal dose is clinician-controlled and not stored

claim: Lactate 2 mmol/L or more marks hypoperfusion; repeat lactate after resuscitation (2-4 hours)
source: Surviving Sepsis Campaign 2021; Sepsis-3

claim: Positive pregnancy test with pain: ectopic pregnancy until proven otherwise; ultrasound, avoid CT
source: NICE NG126; WSES appendicitis 2020

claim: Penicillin allergy: record the exact reaction; choose the antibiotic by the hospital rule
source: BSACI beta-lactam guideline; NICE CG183

claim: Anaphylaxis: stop the drug, call for help, IM adrenaline 500 micrograms repeated after 5 minutes if no improvement, oxygen, IV crystalloid bolus 500-1000 mL in an adult
source: Resuscitation Council UK anaphylaxis guideline (PDF read)

claim: Anticoagulant and antiplatelet plans; never stop dual antiplatelets after a recent stent without the heart team
source: UKCPA Handbook; PAUSE (V-08)

claim: Diabetes plan, steroid cover, GLP-1 and SGLT2 handling, fasting times, unknown fasting means full stomach and rapid sequence induction
source: CPOC; NICE NG243; ASA 2023 fasting; NAP4

claim: A capable patient may refuse surgery; antibiotics-only is a recognised option for simple appendicitis without a stone, with a recurrence risk; document and give safety-net advice
source: APPAC trial and WSES 2020; GMC consent guidance

claim: Deterioration during transfer: stop, ABCDE, call for help
source: RCUK ABCDE approach; ICS and WFSA transfer principles
